1. Case 1: Borderline phyllodes tumor, The 73-year-old woman presents with a palpable left breast mass. Ultrasound shows a circumscribed oval mass with heterogeneous stiffness (BI-RADS 4a). Histopathology reveals pleomorphic spindle cells, CD34 positivity, Ki-67 15%, and clear margins. Elevated Ki-67 and pleomorphism exclude benign lesions; circumscribed margins and CD34 favor phyllodes over sarcoma. The leading hypothesis is phyllodes tumor/borderline stromal neoplasm (score 0.82), refined to borderline phyllodes tumor (score 0.78). Malignant phyllodes (0.18) and sarcoma (0.10) remain less likely, while benign lesions are effectively ruled out. Therefore, the most likely diagnosis is borderline phyllodes tumor.

Definitive confirmation awaits pleural fluid cytology and biopsy pathology, so confidence is moderate.
